title: Anthropic's Internal Use of Claude AI Grew 250x to Support Research on New Models
summary:
The monthly utility of the Claude AI models' internal usage surpassed Anthropic's total expenditure on human staff in April as the firm expanded its use of automation for core research and engineering. According to an updated S-1 registration statement filed with the SEC on Nov. 2, the startup saw the internal use of its models grow more than 250 times over an eight month period. This internal scaling precedes a warning in the filing that future models could soon meet a threshold for "dramatically accelerated progress," defined as AI capabilities improving at roughly twice the pace of models developed without substantial automation.

While no current model has officially crossed that line, Anthropic is considering updates to its Responsible Scaling Policy to require human approval for certain R&D decisions to prevent the autonomous development of frontier models. The startup also amended its filing to state that capabilities "may have already advanced" at a rate requiring enhanced safety measures, compared to a previous draft that said they "could advance." In the same filing, the AI lab reported that Q3 revenue reached $17B, a 12x increase from the prior year.

selectedTweets.text:
Anthropic updated its S1 this morning. Notable additions re automated AI R&D and human oversight of it:

"[...] our internal estimates and our expectations regarding future models, rather than our current models, indicate that we may imminently meet our Responsible Scaling Policy’s definition of 'dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI.' We have not designated any of our current models as exceeding this threshold, and we continue to assess the underlying data. We are also evaluating the implications of meeting the AI research and development capability threshold and will release further reports in the future as we set forth in our Responsible Scaling Policy."

"We are also considering additional measures, including updates to our Responsible Scaling Policy, to require human review and approval of certain decisions in our research and development processes as our models perform an increasing share of that work."

"We believe our investments in safety techniques will enable us to manage these risks and responsibly realize substantially more leverage from Claude than we do today in developing AI models. However, we do not anticipate being able to safely use Claude to fully autonomously design and build successive generations of frontier models without meaningful human supervision or understanding, if and when that becomes technically possible. Accordingly, we are considering updates to our Responsible Scaling Policy to keep humans in control of frontier model development at Anthropic."

selectedTweets.text:
Anthropic says in its amended S-1 that its internal estimates and expectations about FUTURE models indicate that it may "imminently" meet the definition if "dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI".

Under the RSP, this means that Anthropic observes or expects 2x the rate of progress in AI capabilities vs. the rate Anthropic would expect and the fastest rate of extended progress observed over at least 3 model generations without significant AI contributions to AI R&D, plus it's plausible that this doubling is due to automation of research and/or engineering such that it's likely that there will be even greater acceleration.

Note that "2x the rate of progress" means that 2 years of progress would be compressed into 1 year.  So, if Anthropic would have improved its models 9x in one year without AI-enabled acceleration, this threshold would be reached when Anthropic expects to be able to improve its models by 81x in one year (9^2).

selectedTweets.text:
AI researcher @herbiebradley explains what Anthropic may be seeing internally as it approaches a major milestone in recursive self-improving AI:

"They have their latest generation of models, which is not yet released, and I expect they're seeing much greater aggregate researcher and engineer productivity uplifts."

"We would benefit from much more high-resolution reporting from the labs of exactly what types of productivity uplifts they're seeing."

"The threshold they refer to in their S1 is a 2X overall productivity uplift. They expect to achieve this with a near future model, or imminently was the term."

"It translates into R of around naught point five, where R equals one is a fully self-sustaining acceleration loop. So we don't have a fully self-sustaining loop, but they designate the threshold as concerning enough to report."
